title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 138 (Release of one co-surety does not discharge others)

content.overview: Section 138 provides that where there are co-sureties, a release by the creditor of one of them does not discharge the others; neither does it free the surety so released from his responsibility to the other sureties.
content.glance: Release of one co-surety does not discharge the others, nor free the released surety from responsibility to the remaining co-sureties.
content.study: Where there are co-sureties, a release by the creditor of one of them does not discharge the others; neither does it free the surety so released from his responsibility to the other sureties. Current-law framing: co-surety contribution rights under Sections 146–147 remain relevant between the sureties.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: Where there are co-sureties, a release by the creditor of one of them does not discharge the others; neither does it free the surety so released from his responsibility to the other sureties.

examples.title: Release of one co-surety
examples.body: Creditor releases one of several co-sureties. The remaining co-sureties stay liable to the creditor, and the released surety remains responsible to the others.

hypotheticals.question: There are three co-sureties. The creditor releases one. Are the other two discharged?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 138 provides that release of one co-surety does not discharge the others.
